title: Write the story before the slides
description: A sample deck about writing decks, built from every layout Deck offers.

slides.title: Write the story before the slides
slides.subtitle: A short guide to this format, written in the format itself. Replace every word when you write the real one.
slides.notes:
Open with the one thing you want the room to remember.
Press N to hide these notes, F for full screen.

slides.text: A deck is one argument told in order, and every slide earns its place by moving it forward.
slides.notes: Say the sentence, then stop. Let it land before you move on.

slides.title: Three parts carry most stories
slides.lead: Name each part by the job it does for the audience, not by what you built.

cards.name: Setup
bullets: Describe the situation in the audience’s own words
Give one number or example that makes it real

cards.name: Turn
bullets: Show the moment the old way stops working
Introduce what you offer as the answer to that moment
Keep it to what they can see, not how it works

cards.name: Ask
cards.role: What you want them to do
bullets: One decision, with a name and a date beside it
Make the first step small enough to say yes to

slides.notes: Point at each card in turn. The accent colours are optional; one colour per idea works well.

slides.title: From draft to the room in five steps

steps.label: Write the sentence
steps.detail: One line the whole deck defends.

steps.label: Outline the turns
steps.detail: A slide for each step of the argument, nothing else.

steps.label: Choose layouts
steps.detail: Pick the layout that fits each slide’s job.

steps.label: Rehearse aloud
steps.detail: Present with notes open and cut what you skip.

steps.label: Share the link
steps.detail: It opens on any screen and prints one slide per page.

slides.notes: Flows read left to right. Three to five steps; the last one is the destination.

slides.title: Show the product, then point at it
slides.alt: The three-card slide from this sample deck
slides.caption: Use a real screenshot and mark only the places you will talk about.

callouts.label: Each card names its role in one line
A card can link onward, here to the ask

slides.notes: Callouts are positioned in percent of the image, so they stay put at any size.

slides.title: Keep numbers few, round and sourced

stats.label: slides in this sample, one per layout
per slide at most when presenting

slides.notes: Big numbers count up when the slide appears. Every number should have a source line.

slides.title: Replace this sample with your story
slides.lead: Keep the layouts and change the words, by hand or with Claude.

steps.text: Copy the layouts you need from this deck
Write notes for every slide you will present
Ask Claude to check it, then share the link

slides.notes: End on the decision. Leave this slide up during questions.
